title: Requests
description: The base URL, the path and query encoding, the headers and the body (clients/spec/README.md, sections 3.1 to 3.3 and 3.9).

cases.description: A GET carries Authorization, Accept application/json, the User-Agent of section 3.9, and no Content-Type or Idempotency-Key.
A POST with a JSON body carries Content-Type application/json and the User-Agent too.
The base URL loses its trailing slash, and its scheme and host go to lower case.
Without an option the client reads OSCAR_BASE_URL.
The base_url option wins over OSCAR_BASE_URL.
With no option and no variable the client uses DEFAULT_BASE_URL, the production origin https://oscaraccountant.com.
http is accepted for a loopback host, with its port.
Each path value is percent-encoded: every byte except A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~.
A path value `..` is a UsageError and nothing is sent: a URL parser would take it as a move up and reach another path.
A path value `.` is a UsageError and nothing is sent: a URL parser would drop the segment.
An empty path value is a UsageError and nothing is sent.
Booleans are true and false, numbers are decimal, dates are YYYY-MM-DD, text is sent as given; a null value is left out.
Query text with reserved characters is encoded so the server reads it back unchanged.
A JSON body holds only the fields the caller set; a field set to null is sent as null.
An optional body the caller does not give is not sent: no body and no Content-Type.
A response field the client does not know does not break it; the JSON result keeps what the models keep.
An enum value the client does not know does not break it (the unknown value fallback).
